checks.claim: Silicon is made by heating quartz sand with carbon in an electric arc furnace at up to about 2,000 degrees Celsius
checks.why: Metallurgical silicon comes from quartz and carbon in a submerged arc furnace whose hot zone is about 2,000 degrees Celsius (reactions from about 1,300 to 2,000).

sources.title: Silicon production in a submerged arc furnace (Metallurgical and Materials Transactions B)
Reactions in the silicon furnace (Metallurgical and Materials Transactions B)

checks.claim: Chips are made from one single silicon crystal pulled slowly from melted silicon (the Czochralski method)
checks.why: In the Czochralski method a seed is dipped into melted silicon and slowly raised, drawing one single-crystal ingot.

sources.title: Methods for forming single crystal silicon ingots (patent describing the Czochralski method)

checks.claim: Cleanrooms for chips blow filtered air down from the ceiling to keep dust off the wafers
checks.why: Chip cleanrooms use HEPA or ULPA filtered air flowing down from the ceiling and out through a raised floor, sweeping particles away.
